fields.label: Statement summary
fields.text: For n-fold repetition where the bank declares the note valid when at least t of n repetitions succeed, the optimal counterfeiting probability equals sum_{t<=j<=n} C(n,j) alpha^j (1-alpha)^{n-j} (eq. 4), with alpha the single-repetition optimum (3/4 for Wiesner). It holds under sum_k p_k |psi_k><psi_k| = (1/d) 1 (eq. 5) and Y = (alpha/d) 1 optimal dual. The paper says this holds for Wiesner's scheme and the other schemes it discusses.

fields.label: Variables
fields.text:
n: repetitions (qubits)
t: required number of successful repetitions
alpha: single-repetition optimal counterfeiting probability

fields.label: Game definition
fields.text: The success event counted per repetition is Q_1 = the counterfeit succeeds for BOTH copies in that repetition, and the attacker wins if the number of such joint successes is >= t (operator R on p.11). This is NOT the realistic noisy game in which each copy separately must pass its own threshold test.

fields.label: Not valid for
items: W2 as defined in the master plan (per-copy threshold verifier, noise, loss)
any honest-noise model: the formula says nothing about honest acceptance
